CheckTitle: Secure redirect URIs protect application registration tokens from interception and theft
Description:
Entra ID **application registrations** must use **secure redirect URIs**. This check flags web, SPA and public-client redirect URIs that use plain `http://` on non-loopback hosts, reside on shared platform domains like `azurewebsites.net`, contain wildcards, or are malformed.

Tokens are delivered to redirect URIs, so insecure URIs expose them to interception or theft.
Risk: An insecure redirect URI allows an attacker to **intercept authorization codes and tokens** in transit (plain HTTP), **redirect them** to a host they control (wildcard or malformed URI), or **claim a dangling subdomain** on a shared platform domain like `azurewebsites.net` to receive valid tokens for the application's users.

Code.Other:
1. Navigate to Microsoft Entra admin center (https://entra.microsoft.com)
2. Go to Applications > App registrations
3. Select the flagged application
4. Go to Authentication
5. Replace any `http://` redirect URIs with `https://`
6. Remove any wildcard URIs and unused or malformed URIs
7. Move applications off `*.azurewebsites.net` onto a custom domain you own
8. Delete redirect URIs whose domain no longer resolves in DNS

Recommendation.Text: Use only `https://` redirect URIs pointing to domains you own and control. Remove **wildcard** entries, replace shared platform domains with **custom domains**, and clean up unused or malformed URIs to prevent token theft via redirect manipulation or subdomain takeover.

Notes: DNS resolution checks for dangling domains are not performed by this check due to network egress requirements, non-deterministic results, and false positives on internal-only hostnames. Custom URI schemes used by public clients (msal://, ms-appx-web://, brk-://, urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob, com.company.app://) are excluded from validation. Loopback hosts (localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]) are allowed over plain HTTP per Microsoft's platform behaviour.
